# `silk/core/schedule`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Schedules: policies that say when to run an effect again, and when to stop.

## When to use
Use a [`Schedule`](#Schedule) to retry a failed effect with a delay, or to repeat an effect on a timer.
The drivers are `Effect.retry`, `Effect.retryWhile` and `Effect.repeat` in `silk.core.effect`.

| Constructor | Delay before recurrence `n` (from 0) |
|---|---|
| [`Schedule.spaced`](#Schedule.impl.spaced) | the same delay each time, counted from the end of the last run |
| [`Schedule.fixed`](#Schedule.impl.fixed) | the time to the next multiple of the interval since the start |
| [`Schedule.exponential`](#Schedule.impl.exponential) | `base * 2^n` |
| [`Schedule.exponentialBy`](#Schedule.impl.exponentialBy) | `base * factor^n` |
| [`Schedule.fibonacci`](#Schedule.impl.fibonacci) | `base`, `base`, `2 * base`, `3 * base`, `5 * base`, ... |
| [`Schedule.linear`](#Schedule.impl.linear) | `base * (n + 1)` |
| [`Schedule.forever`](#Schedule.impl.forever) | no delay, with no limit |
| [`Schedule.recurs`](#Schedule.impl.recurs) | no delay, at most `times` recurrences |

[`Schedule.limit`](#Schedule.impl.limit), [`Schedule.capDelay`](#Schedule.impl.capDelay), [`Schedule.upTo`](#Schedule.impl.upTo), [`Schedule.jittered`](#Schedule.impl.jittered) and
[`Schedule.jitteredBetween`](#Schedule.impl.jitteredBetween) change a schedule.

## Details
A Schedule is a plain value. It holds no clock and no progress, so one value can drive any
number of runs. A driver keeps the progress of one run in a [`ScheduleState`](#ScheduleState) that
[`Schedule.start`](#Schedule.impl.start) makes, and asks [`Schedule.next`](#Schedule.impl.next) for each delay. A custom driver, such as
one that honours a server's `Retry-After`, uses the same two operations.

Durations are `u64` nanoseconds, so a duration literal such as `250ms` works.

## Gotchas
- A recurrence is a run after the first one. `Schedule.recurs(3)` with `Effect.repeat` runs the
  effect four times, and with `Effect.retry` makes at most four attempts.
- Jitter draws from the `InsecureRandom` effect, so the same seed gives the same delays. The
  drivers require `&mut InsecureRandom` even when the schedule has no jitter.

## Examples
### Repeat on a fixed beat
```silk
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.core.schedule { Schedule }
import silk.system.insecure_random { InsecureRandom }
import silk.system.monotonic_clock { MonotonicClock }
import silk.system.system_clock { Instant, SystemClock }

struct TestClock {
  mark: Instant,
}

impl MonotonicClock for TestClock {
  effect fn now(self: &mut Self) -> Instant {
    return SystemClock.make(SystemClock.seconds(&self.mark), SystemClock.nanoseconds(&self.mark))
  }

  effect fn getResolution(self: &mut Self) -> u64 {
    return 1
  }

  effect fn waitUntil(self: &mut Self, when: Instant) -> () {
    self.mark = move when
    return ()
  }

  effect fn waitFor(self: &mut Self, howLong: u64) -> () {
    self.mark = MonotonicClock.deadlineAfter(&self.mark, howLong)
    return ()
  }
}

struct Beats {
  count: i32,
}

effect fn beat(beats: &mut Beats) -> () {
  beats.count = beats.count + 1
  return ()
}

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let mut clock = TestClock { mark: SystemClock.make(0, 0) }
  let mut random = InsecureRandom.seeded(1)
  let mut beats = Beats { count: 0 }
  // One run, then three more, each on the next 500ms beat.
  let steady = Schedule.fixed(500ms) |> Schedule.limit(3)
  run Effect.repeat(beat(&mut beats), &steady)
    |> Effect.provideMut<InsecureRandom>(&mut random)
    |> Effect.provideMut<MonotonicClock>(&mut clock)
  if beats.count != 4 || SystemClock.seconds(&clock.mark) != 1 || SystemClock.nanoseconds(&clock.mark) != 500000000 {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

## `Schedule`

```silk
pub struct Schedule
```

A policy that says how long to wait before each recurrence, and when to stop.

### When to use

Pass a Schedule to `Effect.retry`, `Effect.retryWhile` or `Effect.repeat`. Make one with a
constructor such as [`Schedule.spaced`](#Schedule.impl.spaced) or [`Schedule.exponential`](#Schedule.impl.exponential), and change it with
[`Schedule.limit`](#Schedule.impl.limit), [`Schedule.capDelay`](#Schedule.impl.capDelay), [`Schedule.upTo`](#Schedule.impl.upTo) or [`Schedule.jittered`](#Schedule.impl.jittered).

### Details

A Schedule holds no progress, so one value can drive any number of runs. Durations are `u64`
nanoseconds.

### Examples

#### Back off exponentially, at most five times
```silk
import silk.core.schedule { Schedule }

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let policy = Schedule.exponential(100ms) |> Schedule.capDelay(2s) |> Schedule.limit(5)
  drop policy
  return 0
}
```

<a id="ScheduleState"></a>

## `ScheduleState`

```silk
pub struct ScheduleState
```

The progress of one run of a [`Schedule`](#Schedule): how many recurrences it has made, and when it began.

### When to use

Only a driver needs it. Make one with [`Schedule.start`](#Schedule.impl.start) when the run begins, and pass it to
each [`Schedule.next`](#Schedule.impl.next) of the same run.

<a id="Schedule.impl.forever"></a>

### Associated function `forever`

```silk
pub fn forever() -> Schedule
```

Recurs with no delay and no limit.

#### Gotchas

`Effect.repeat` with this schedule never stops unless the effect fails, and `Effect.retry`
never stops unless the effect succeeds. Add [`Schedule.limit`](#Schedule.impl.limit) or [`Schedule.upTo`](#Schedule.impl.upTo) to stop.

<a id="Schedule.impl.recurs"></a>

### Associated function `recurs`

```silk
pub fn recurs(times: u64) -> Schedule
```

Recurs with no delay, at most `times` times.

#### Details

With `Effect.repeat`, the effect runs `times + 1` times. With `Effect.retry`, it makes at most
`times + 1` attempts.

<a id="Schedule.impl.spaced"></a>

### Associated function `spaced`

```silk
pub fn spaced(delay: u64) -> Schedule
```

Waits the same `delay` before each recurrence.

#### Details

The delay counts from the end of the run before, so the time the effect takes adds to the
period. Use [`Schedule.fixed`](#Schedule.impl.fixed) to keep a steady beat.

<a id="Schedule.impl.fixed"></a>

### Associated function `fixed`

```silk
pub fn fixed(interval: u64) -> Schedule
```

Recurs on each multiple of `interval` after the start of the run.

#### When to use

Use it for a steady beat, such as a poll every second or a note every eighth of a bar. The
time each run takes does not move later recurrences.

#### Details

Recurrence `n`, counted from 0, is due at `(n + 1) * interval` after [`Schedule.start`](#Schedule.impl.start), and
the delay is the time from now to that beat. If a run ends after its next beat, the
recurrence happens at the first beat that is not past, or at once when the run ends exactly
on a beat. Thus missed beats do not pile up, and a late run does not move later beats. An
`interval` of 0 recurs at once.

#### Gotchas

[`Schedule.jittered`](#Schedule.impl.jittered) moves each recurrence off its beat by the jitter.

<a id="Schedule.impl.exponential"></a>

### Associated function `exponential`

```silk
pub fn exponential(base: u64) -> Schedule
```

Waits `base * 2^n` before recurrence `n`, counted from 0.

#### Details

The delay is computed in `f64`. A delay that is more than a `u64` can hold becomes `u64.MAX`.

<a id="Schedule.impl.exponentialBy"></a>

### Associated function `exponentialBy`

```silk
pub fn exponentialBy(base: u64, factor: f64) -> Schedule
```

Waits `base * factor^n` before recurrence `n`, counted from 0.

#### Details

A `factor` between 0 and 1 makes the delays shorter each time. A delay that is more than a
`u64` can hold becomes `u64.MAX`.

<a id="Schedule.impl.fibonacci"></a>

### Associated function `fibonacci`

```silk
pub fn fibonacci(base: u64) -> Schedule
```

Waits `base` times the next Fibonacci number: `base`, `base`, `2 * base`, `3 * base`, ...

<a id="Schedule.impl.linear"></a>

### Associated function `linear`

```silk
pub fn linear(base: u64) -> Schedule
```

Waits `base * (n + 1)` before recurrence `n`, counted from 0.

<a id="Schedule.impl.limit"></a>

### Method `limit`

```silk
pub fn limit(self: Schedule, times: u64) -> Schedule
```

Stops `self` after at most `times` recurrences.

#### Details

When `self` already has a smaller limit, that limit stays.

<a id="Schedule.impl.capDelay"></a>

### Method `capDelay`

```silk
pub fn capDelay(self: Schedule, most: u64) -> Schedule
```

Makes each delay of `self` at most `most`.

#### Details

The cap applies after jitter. When `self` already has a smaller cap, that cap stays.

<a id="Schedule.impl.upTo"></a>

### Method `upTo`

```silk
pub fn upTo(self: Schedule, howLong: u64) -> Schedule
```

Stops `self` when `howLong` has passed since the start of the run.

#### Details

The check happens before each recurrence. A run that is already in progress is not stopped.
When `self` already has a shorter time, that time stays.

<a id="Schedule.impl.jittered"></a>

### Method `jittered`

```silk
pub fn jittered(self: Schedule) -> Schedule
```

Multiplies each delay of `self` by a random factor between 0.8 and 1.2.

#### When to use

Use it so that many clients that retry at the same time spread out.

<a id="Schedule.impl.jitteredBetween"></a>

### Method `jitteredBetween`

```silk
pub fn jitteredBetween(self: Schedule, min: f64, max: f64) -> Schedule
```

Multiplies each delay of `self` by a random factor between `min` and `max`.

#### Details

The factor is uniform in `[min, max)`, from one `InsecureRandom.nextU64` for each delay. Give
`min` at most `max`, and both at least 0: a delay below 0 becomes 0.

<a id="Schedule.impl.start"></a>

### Method `start`

```silk
pub fn start(self: &Schedule, now: Instant) -> ScheduleState
```

Begins one run of `self` at `now`.

#### When to use

Only a driver needs it. Read the clock when the run begins, before the first run of the
effect, and pass the state to each [`Schedule.next`](#Schedule.impl.next) of the run.

<a id="Schedule.impl.next"></a>

### Method `next`

```silk
pub effect fn next(self: &Schedule, state: &mut ScheduleState, now: &Instant) -> Option<u64>
    ? &mut InsecureRandom
```

Decides the next recurrence of a run: the delay to wait before it, or `None` to stop.

#### Details

Pass the time of the decision as `now`. A `Some` counts one recurrence in `state`. The draw
from `InsecureRandom` happens only when `self` has jitter.
